proposed.explanation:
RANKING BY P/E (lower = cheaper) and PROFIT GROWTH (higher = better):

P/E (using latest EPS vs. current price):
1. ABUK ≈ 6.5× (annualised 9M-2026 EPS 8.74 × 12/9 = 11.65; price 76.21)
2. EFID ≈ 9.4× (FY2025 EPS 2.18; price 20.40)
3. TMGH ≈ 11.8× (FY2025 EPS 6.98; price 82.50)
4. ETEL ≈ 11.9× (FY2025 EPS 11.93; price 141.95)

Profit growth (YoY):
1. ETEL: EPS +149% (4.79 → 11.93). NOTE: the printed net-profit line shows 578,063,000 EGP for 2025 vs 10,111,328,000 EGP for 2024 (a –94% decline), which is internally inconsistent with the EPS increase. I flag this as a data-quality concern; the EPS trajectory is the more reliable per-share signal, but the discrepancy should be investigated before a large position.
2. ABUK: 9M EPS +104% (4.28 → 8.74). Data covers only 9 months ended Sep-2026, so the full-year picture is incomplete.
3. EFID: net profit +68% (1,606,727,698 → 2,695,301,670 EGP); EPS +100% (1.09 → 2.18).
4. TMGH: net profit +43% (12,769,517,325 → 18,201,981,482 EGP); EPS +59% (4.38 → 6.98).

SUGGESTED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP, medium risk, 7+ yr horizon):

• EFID – 1,470 sh × 20.40 = 29,988 EGP (≈30%)
• TMGH – 363 sh × 82.50 = 29,947.50 EGP (≈30%)
• ABUK – 262 sh × 76.21 = 19,967.02 EGP (≈20%)
• ETEL – 140 sh × 141.95 = 19,873.00 EGP (≈20%)

Total invested: 99,775.52 EGP; residual cash ≈ 224 EGP.
No single position exceeds 50% of the 100,000 EGP portfolio.

Rationale for weighting: EFID and TMGH get the larger 30% slots because they have clean, full-year audited results with strong, consistent growth. ABUK is attractive on P/E and growth but only 9-month data is available, so I cap it at 20%. ETEL is also capped at 20% because of the net-profit/EPS inconsistency in the FY2025 report; I would want to see the next interim or a clarification before adding more.

RISKS & UNCERTAINTY:
- ABUK's P/E is annualised from 9-month data; actual full-year EPS could differ.
- ETEL's FY2025 net-profit figure appears inconsistent with its EPS; treat the valuation with caution until clarified.
- All four are Egyptian-listed names; currency, regulatory, and market-liquidity risks apply.
- Past growth does not guarantee future performance. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
